ETH+.$kindComment: Reserve RToken, basket of ETH LSTs. Measured on-chain 2026-07-31: basketsNeeded/totalSupply = 4162.403/3806.244 = 1.0936 (>1) and no rebase() entry point, so the balance is static and value accrues through the redemption rate. That single sample shows the level, not the trend, though the ratio is monotone in practice: measured 1.0912985 -> 1.0929479 -> 1.0935725 at blocks 25508413/25608413/25658413, rising across both an issuance and a redemption leg because basketsNeeded moves proportionally with supply. It can still fall on a collateral haircut.

ezETH.$kindComment: Renzo ezETH; rate from RestakeManager (per feed config).
ezETH.$comment: Finding #2: ezETH's primary is fundamental (Renzo RestakeManager) and its only monitor, ezETHCrossRate, is ALSO fundamental after the 2026-07-22 migration to RedStone's ezETH_FUNDAMENTAL feed - so the 250 bps tolerance could not fire on a market depeg. ezETHCrossRateMarket adds a genuine MARKET leg (RedStone Classic Push ezETH/ETH). Both monitors are kept: divergenceBps is primary-vs-the-WORST-single-monitor (not the median), so the market monitor DOMINATES rather than being diluted by the fundamental one sitting near 0 bps. Its 46800 heartbeat is derived from the feed's measured 12 h cadence (max gap 43224 s + 3576 s margin), NOT copied from ezETHCrossRate's 86400; the registered value must cover the slower leg because TwoFeedChainlinkPriceFeed reports updatedAt = min(rateUpdatedAt, baseUpdatedAt), and the 12 h rate leg is slower than WETH's 3600 s ETH/USD. See custom-price-feeds/1.json.ezETHCrossRateMarket for the full measurement and the deprecated-feed rationale.

rsETH.$kindComment: Kelp rsETH; rate from rateProvider (per feed config).

ETHx.$kindComment: Stader ETHx; rate from stakePoolsManager (per feed config).
ETHx.note: MONITOR FEEDS REWORKED 2026-07-27 for Redstone's ETHx sunset. Redstone is retiring BOTH of its ETHx push feeds, which backed both of ETHx's monitors. (1) The direct Redstone ETHx/USD monitor (0xFaBEb1474C2Ab34838081BFdDcE4132f640E7D2d) is REMOVED with no replacement — Chainlink has no ETHx/USD feed (FeedRegistry.getFeed reverts "Feed not found"). (2) The ETHxCrossRate monitor SURVIVES: its underlying ETHx/ETH rate feed was migrated from Redstone to the Chainlink ETHx/ETH feed 0xC499ec76e2F5ac15e127A352Bc40cF24FC472401 (see contracts-deployment-config/custom-price-feeds/1.json). So ETHx keeps ONE monitor and retains its divergence/irregular signal at the 250 bps tolerance. The PRIMARY price was never affected: ETHx_CustomPriceFeed reads Stader's on-chain rate via stakePoolsManager, no Redstone dependency.

osETH.$kindComment: StakeWise osETH; rate from osTokenVaultController (per feed config).
osETH.note: Priced via osToken_CustomPriceFeed (priceFeeds.osETH.1): convertToAssets(1e18) [osETH/ETH] * ETH/USD. Held osETH is reported by ERC20DefaultBalanceAdapter (wallet balance). The pricefeed address is filled by 03_DeployPriceFeeds. Separate from the StakeWiseV3Vault osToken-debt leg (denominated in ETH).

EURC.$kindComment: FLAG: EUR fiat-backed. Pegged in mechanism but NOT to the NAV quote asset (USD), so Floating under the stated rule.

stETH.$kindComment: Lido staked ETH; stETH/ETH held at 1.0 by the redemption invariant (per feed config) and yield delivered as balance growth.
stETH.$comment: Finding #1: stETH was the only ETH-LST whose PRIMARY was a market feed, while wstETH and eETH - the same underlying claim - are priced fundamental. During a stETH discount the two disagreed by the full discount and irregularPriceAssets flagged wstETH but not stETH, which reads backwards. Primary is now the fundamental unit-rate feed; the market stETH/ETH cross-rate is retained as a monitor so divergenceBps becomes meaningful for stETH for the first time. Heartbeat stays 86400 to match wstETH/weETH/eETH; it is looser than WETH's 3600 base, which is safe because NavBaseUsdLib inherits the base's own staleness verdict regardless, so a looser derived heartbeat cannot over-report.

lsETH.$kindComment: Liquid Collective lsETH; Chainlink 'LsETH / ETH Exchange Rate' (per feed config).

sUSDe.$kindComment: Staked USDe share; balance static, rate grows with funding yield.

sUSDS.$kindComment: ERC-4626 share of USDS; balance static, rate grows.
sUSDS.$comment: Finding #8: heartbeat raised 82800 -> 86400 to match its own base asset USDS. Post-ADR-0019 this feed's latestRoundData().updatedAt IS the USDS/USD feed's timestamp (ERC4626VaultRatePriceFeed._compute -> NavBaseUsdLib.baseUsd), and _selectFeedCore gates that timestamp against the heartbeat registered HERE. So a derived feed gated tighter than its base cannot prevent a stale price - it can only manufacture a stale verdict while the base is still fresh. Measured on the USDS/USD aggregator 0x592700e4FcDd674dC54d2681DED3B63f54F63f9A over 58 days (61 intervals, rounds 2483-2544): the publisher is heartbeat-driven on a ~23h cadence and 59 of 61 intervals overshot 82800 by a median 24s (max 72s), so sUSDS was priced $0 and listed in stalePriceAssets for ~23s a day, on 97% of days, while USDS itself never went stale (max gap 82872 < 86400). 86400 restores the same 3600s of margin the base carries. sUSDS has a single primary feed, so there is no second feed to rescue the read. Do NOT tighten the reverse direction (wstETH/stETH/lsETH/weETH/eETH/OETH/LDO at 86400 over WETH's 3600): a looser derived heartbeat cannot over-report, because NavBaseUsdLib inherits the base's own staleness verdict regardless.

OETH.$kindComment: Origin ETH; rebasing to holders, priced via a market OETH/ETH cross-rate. accrualKind describes the TOKEN, not this system's positions: Origin's OToken auto-migrates CONTRACT holders to non-rebasing on their first balance-changing interaction, and that has already happened to a registered account here - ACCOUNT_11 (0x0EFcCBb9E2C09Ea29551879bd9Da32362b32fc89) carries nonRebasingCreditsPerToken = 1e18 with rebaseState = NotSet, i.e. auto-classified with nobody opting out. So do NOT infer balance growth for a Safe's OETH position from Rebasing. No registered account held OETH when this was measured (mainnet block 25656631; 36% of OETH supply was non-rebasing).
